NeatMS is an open source python package for untargeted LCMS signal labelling and filtering.
NeatMS enables automated filtering of false positive MS1 peaks reported by commonly used LCMS data processing pipelines.
NeatMS relies on neural network based classification.
NeatMS is distributed as an open source software under the MIT License.
The neural network output uses a softmax activation function that produces a probability distribution of 3 probabilities between 0 and 1.
The 3 probabilities in the neural network output add up to 1, with one probability per class.

At a 0.01 probability threshold, 100% of High_quality peaks would be correctly predicted but 44% would be false positives. At a 0.01 threshold, 80% of Low_quality peaks would be predicted as High_qual
If correctly trained, a model should obtain an AUC higher than 95.0.
The matrix size argument represents the number of points used to represent a peak.
The margin argument represents the size of the surrounding signal that should be kept on the retention time dimension.
A margin of 1 means that the margin size on both sides of the peak will be the same size as the peak width.
For a peak with a retention time width of 3 seconds and margin of 1, the extracted signal will be 9 seconds.
With default argument values, the first and last 40 values of the peak represent the margins, and the middle 40 values represent the peak itself.
A second dimension is added to represent the margin portion of the signal (0) or the peak signal (1).
The resulting matrix size for one peak is (2, 120) with default arguments.
Changing the matrix size or margin argument will automatically adapt the neural network architecture.
When using transfer learning on a preexisting model, one should not change the matrix size or margin arguments if intending to use the default model.
The min_scan_number argument filters out peaks with fewer points than the specified value.
The default min_scan_number value is 5 because it is difficult to judge if a signal is a peak when it has less than 5 points.
A model and the person who trained it will likely underperform for peaks with fewer than 5 points.
The min_scan_number argument has no impact on the model architecture.
When using an existing model, lowering the min_scan_number parameter is strongly advised against. Increasing the min_scan_number parameter when using an existing model is not a problem.
Three batches of data are required for neural network training: one for training, one for testing, and one for validation.
The training and test sets are used during the training process while the validation set remains untouched for hyperparameter tuning.
The default split between training:test:validation batches is 80:10:10.
The validation_split argument allows definition of the size of test and validation sets.
The validation_split argument should not exceed 0.2 to ensure at least 60% of data is left for training.
The normalise_class argument ensures every class has the same number of peaks for training.
When normalise_class is set to True, the number of peaks for each class equals the smallest class.
Full model training is recommended when there are at least 500 peaks for each class.
